title: Homotopical injectivity of sheaf dg modules
statement: Let $S$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on a small site, and let $A$ be a sheaf dg $S$-algebra. Use the signed left dg module conventions of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization], interpreted sheafwise on this site: $A$ is an integer cochain complex of $S$-module sheaves on this site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with associative unital $S$-bilinear multiplication and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d_A(b)$; a left dg $A$-module $M$ is such a complex with a unital associative $S$-bilinear action and $d_M(am)=d_A(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d_M(m)$. For left dg modules $M,I$, write $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(M,I)$ for the abelian group of families of $S$-linear sheaf maps $h^i:M^i\to I^{i+r}$, for all $i\in\mathbb Z$, satisfying $h(am)=(-1)^{r|a|}a\,h(m)$ on homogeneous local sections. These are global sheaf morphisms, compatible with restriction on every object of the site, with no finite-support condition in $i$. Give these groups the differential $\delta_r(h)=d_Ih-(-1)^rhd_M$. A left dg $A$-module $I$ is homotopically injective if, for every left dg $A$-module $M$ whose underlying cohomology sheaves all vanish, the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,I)$ is acyclic. Explicitly, for every $r\in\mathbb Z$ and $h\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(M,I)$ with $\delta_r(h)=0$, there exists $g\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{r-1}(M,I)$ with $\delta_{r-1}(g)=h$. Here vanishing cohomology sheaves means $\ker(d_M^i)=\operatorname{im}(d_M^{i-1})$ as subsheaves for every $i$, not exactness on sections over every object. No boundedness, graded injectivity, or exactness of global sections is part of this predicate.

Acyclicity of Hom^•(M,I) for every acyclic M is equivalent to Stacks' Hom_K(M,I)=0, because M[-r] is acyclic exactly when M is. The Lean IsHomotopicallyInjective (read only) is the same predicate.
